sec: Other causes: Cushing, apparent mineralocorticoid excess, GRA · p824

items.q: Match the other causes of saline-unresponsive alkalosis to their immediate mechanism — 1) Cushing syndrome  2) Apparent mineralocorticoid excess  3) Glucocorticosteroid remediable aldosteronism … A) ACTH → aldosterone  B) Cortisol excess  C) Cortisol ✗→ cortisone block
items.exp: Other causes: Cushing syndrome → cortisol excess; apparent mineralocorticoid excess → the cortisol-to-cortisone step is blocked; glucocorticosteroid remediable aldosteronism → ACTH → aldosterone. (Book p824)

items.q: In all three ‘other causes’, the final common pathway printed is:
items.exp: Cushing syndrome gives cortisol excess → mineralocorticoid excess; the AME block also gives mineralocorticoid excess; GRA acts through ACTH → aldosterone. (Book p824)

items.q: In apparent mineralocorticoid excess, which enzymatic conversion is blocked?
items.exp: The block shown is cortisol ✗→ cortisone, so cortisol accumulates and acts as a mineralocorticoid. (Book p824)

items.q: A young patient has hypertension, hypokalemic alkalosis, low renin, low aldosterone and a normal urine chloride; spirolactone works but the family history shows an autosomal dominant trait driven by ACTH. Which cause is printed?
opts: Apparent mineralocorticoid excess with a blocked cortisol-to-cortisone step
Liddle syndrome with a gain-of-function ENaC mutation
Primary hyperaldosteronism with a unilateral adrenal adenoma
items.exp: Glucocorticosteroid remediable aldosteronism acts through ACTH → aldosterone and sits in the ‘other causes’ group of saline-unresponsive alkalosis. (Book p824)

items.q: ‘In Cushing syndrome the alkalosis is driven by cortisol excess producing mineralocorticoid excess.’
opts: False — Cushing syndrome causes alkalosis through renin excess
False — Cushing syndrome causes a metabolic acidosis
True, but only when aldosterone is also high
items.exp: Cushing syndrome: cortisol excess → mineralocorticoid excess, one of the ‘other causes’ of saline-unresponsive metabolic alkalosis. (Book p824)

items.q: All but one of these belong to the ‘other causes’ group of the alkalosis flowchart. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Renin-secreting tumours sit in the ↑renin/↑aldosterone ‘major causes’ column; the ‘other causes’ group contains Cushing syndrome, AME and GRA. (Book p824)
